subject: Medical data boundary question — BAA and deployment options
messages:
From: Joanna Park <joanna.park@medicline.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medicline.com
Date: Fri, 17 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on medical data boundary and BAA for hybrid setup

Hi Monica,

Quick question from our security team as we evaluate Redwood for a pilot: we have a mixed architecture where patient images and PHI will remain in our VPC and on-prem object storage, but we want to use Redwood's inference for NLP scoring and notes normalization.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can process requests where PHI is routed only through our Dedicated/Private deployment (control plane in your cloud but inference in our VPC) without Redwood persisting PHI outside the customer's footprint?
- If you will sign a BAA for that configuration and what your expected process/timeline is?
- What evidence you can provide up front (SOC 2 report, key management details, encryption-at-rest specifics) to accelerate our security review?

Also attaching a short workflow summary we promised the SEC team. Appreciate a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Joanna Park
Director, Security Engineering
MedicLine Health

Attachment: medicline_workflow_summary.pdf (application/pdf, 78KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on medical data boundary and BAA for hybrid setup

Hi Joanna — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the workflow doc. Looping in Neha from Compliance and Laura from Solutions so we can give a complete answer.

High level answers up front:
- Redwood supports Private/VPC and Dedicated models that keep inference within a customer-managed boundary; for hybrid deployments it is possible for PHI to remain in your VPC if you choose our Private package and configure the inference nodes inside your network.
- We do offer a standard BAA for Dedicated and Private customers; we cannot sign a BAA for the hosted public API.
- Evidence we can provide immediately: recent SOC 2 Type II summary, a short KMS/encryption factsheet, and a draft BAA for review. For the final scope we’ll need a few specifics about what payload types contain PHI and whether any outputs will be stored outside your boundary.

Next steps I propose: 1) Neha to list required evidence and any DPIA/processing notes; 2) Rishi to coordinate contract/BAA draft; 3) Laura to follow up on architecture options and a short runbook for deployment. If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute call next week — propose Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

I’m attaching our BAA request form to capture scope details.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_baa_request_form.pdf (application/pdf, 24KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Joanna Park <joanna.park@medicline.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 18 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on medical data boundary and BAA for hybrid setup

Hi Joanna — Neha from Compliance here. Below are clarifications and an evidence checklist to help MedicLine's security review.

Short answers:
- PHI residency: For Redwood Private or dedicated nodes deployed inside your VPC/on-prem, we can ensure inference happens in your environment and that persistent storage of model outputs is optional and configurable (controlled by you). We will not persist PHI in Redwood-hosted shared storage for Private/Dedicated customers unless explicitly configured.
- BAA: Redwood executes our standard BAA for customers running PHI in Dedicated or Private deployments. The process: receipt of your scope questionnaire -> draft BAA -> redlines -> signature (DocuSign) — typical 2–3 week cadence if we have the scope details.

Key technical controls we will provide evidence for:
- Transmission: TLS 1.2+ for all in-transit channels and mutual TLS available for private peering.
- At-rest encryption: AES-256 by default. For Private/Dedicated you can provision your own KMS keys (bring-your-own-key) or use our KMS integration; HSM-backed keys are supported for enterprise plans.
- Key management: Customer-managed keys supported; rotation policies and access separation documented.
- Access controls & auditing: RBAC, role separation, token-based access, and detailed audit logs for inference requests and admin actions. Logs can be exported to your logging stack (S3/GCS/ELK) per retention requirements.
- Data minimization: We recommend you redact or tokenize patient identifiers where possible; we can help with guidance during integration.

Requested items from MedicLine to scope the BAA:
1) Example payloads (sample redacted JSON) indicating which fields are PHI
2) Expected persistent storage behavior (do you want outputs persisted outside your VPC?)
3) Regions and whether any backups cross regions
4) Contact for legal to receive BAA draft and negotiator contact

Evidence we are attaching now: encryption/KMS factsheet and our SOC 2 summary. After we receive the scope questionnaire we will generate a draft BAA and pull together a short DPIA note for your records.

Happy to get on a call to walk through technical controls — please propose times.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Trust & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: encryption_kms_factsheet.pdf (application/pdf, 15KB); redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB)
